newsitem.title: THAILAND: All 65 trapped workers in Thai blaze rescued.
newsitem.headline: All 65 trapped workers in Thai blaze rescued.

text.p: Thai police said on Sunday 65 people trapped on the top floor of a blazing central Bangkok building had been rescued and there were no more people in the 36-storey structure.

"We have rescued 65 people who were trapped in the fire on the top floor. There are no more people trapped in the building now," national police chief General Pracha Promnok told reporters. Earlier, police said two people were killed in the blaze, which broke out on Sunday morning.
Police said up to seven helicopters had been used to ferry the workers to safety from the top floor of the building during the rescue operation, which last nearly four hours.
The fire in the building had been brought under control, but it was unclear if it was completely extinguished. Firefighters were now inspecting the scene, they added.

Construction of the building named President Tower, next to a hotel, had been completed and interior decoration work was going on when the fire broke out on the sixth or seventh floor. The building had been due to open soon, rescue officials said.

Police said that before the fire erupted two loud explosions were heard from the seventh floor of the building, where workers were installing air-conditioners. An investigation was under way to determine the cause of the blaze.
